The highest-value innovations of the world’s top R&D firms*

Which Scoreboard innovations and which Scoreboard firms score highest on knowledge spillovers, marginal returns and private value — and what those innovations are

Data tool for Samuel Edet, Ralf Martin, Golvine de Rochambeau, Trang Thu Tran and Dennis Verhoeven (2026), “Innovation partnerships for development along green value chains”

12 October 2026

* This data tool accompanies the paper “Innovation partnerships for development along green value chains” by Samuel Edet, Ralf Martin, Golvine de Rochambeau, Trang Thu Tran and Dennis Verhoeven (2026), and is powered by the Innovation Strategy Explorer database.

What this page shows

The paper argues that the leading R&D investors of the EU JRC Scoreboard produce the most valuable innovations and account for half of all HIC–EMDE collaborative innovation. This page puts faces to those numbers. For every measure the paper uses — knowledge spillovers accruing globally, to HIC inventors and to EMDE inventors; the marginal return index on each; and the private value of the innovation — it lists the 20 highest-scoring innovations linked to a Scoreboard firm and the 20 firms with the highest average across their innovations. Each innovation comes with the firm, the inventor team’s country composition, the patent title and abstract, and a link to the full text on Espacenet.

Five samples can be chosen: all Scoreboard innovations; those with at least one inventor based in an EMDE (excluding China, as throughout the paper); those that can be linked to one of the verified EMDE research labs of the EMDERLT tracker — the firm has a verified lab in an EMDE country that appears on the patent, which rules out stray country attributions; and the green subsets of the last two. Spillover values and private values are in USD million per innovation; marginal returns are the ISTRAX index in percent. Definitions are those of the paper and of the Innovation Strategy Explorer.

The highest-scoring innovations

Pick a measure and a sample, then step through the gallery with the arrows, the dots or the left/right keys. Each card is one patent family: a drawing from the patent, a plain-English headline and summary, the patent’s own title (linking to the family on Espacenet), the Scoreboard firm(s) it is linked to, the filing year and publication used, the values on every measure, and the inventor team as a donut of inventors by country; green innovations carry a short note on why they count as green. Every control is mirrored in the page address, so a particular view can be bookmarked or sent as a link. The table view lists the countries on the family’s harmonised PATSTAT record — the same table from which the paper’s HIC, EMDE and China flags are computed, so an “EMDE inventor” tag can always be traced to a marked country — and, below it, the raw inventor headcount and how many of those records carry no country code at all (the harmonisation fills these from the inventor’s other patents, which is where the two views can differ).

Headlines and summaries are non-technical paraphrases written by Claude from the patent’s title and abstract; the drawing is the first figure Google Patents holds for the family (hot-linked; drawings that tesseract judged to be on their side are turned upright, and the rotate button turns a drawing a further quarter turn, remembered in this browser only). “Why it counts as green”: the paper’s green flag comes from the EPO’s Y02/Y04S climate-change classes; the plain-English line is the iseapp technology tag built from them, the codes are the patent’s own Y02/Y04S classes with the EPO’s descriptions. Titles and abstracts are the patent documents’ own, retrieved from Google Patents for one publication of each family; the Espacenet link opens the family’s full record. Countries: every country of an inventor or applicant on the family in the harmonised PATSTAT mapping (iseapp countrymap) — the variable from which the paper’s HIC / EMDE (excl. China) / China flags are built; EMDE countries are marked. The second line gives the raw inventor records and how many carry no country code. “EMDERLT lab”: the firm has a verified lab in an EMDE country on the record.

The firms that do best on average

The same measures averaged over each firm’s innovations in the chosen sample, again as a gallery (arrows, dots or the keyboard) with a table view alongside. Each card gives the firm’s average against the sample average, its number of innovations in the sample and overall, its EMDE share, a donut of the countries its inventors work in (over all of the firm’s 2013–2022 innovations, innovation-weighted or by headcount), and its single best innovation in the sample with drawing and summary. Because a firm with two spectacular patents would otherwise top every list, the menu sets a minimum number of innovations in the sample; 30 is the default.

innovations in the sample
‹
›
Averages are simple means over the firm’s innovations in the chosen sample. “EMDE share” is the share of all the firm’s 2013–2022 innovations that involve an EMDE inventor, the explanatory variable of the paper. The country mix covers all of the firm’s 2013–2022 innovations (pipeline firm × country indicators): innovation-weighted counts each innovation once for every country in which it has an inventor; inventor headcount counts distinct inventors by country of residence. The best innovation is the firm’s single highest-scoring one in the sample on the chosen measure. Drawings that tesseract judged to be on their side are turned upright automatically; the rotate button under a drawing turns it a further quarter turn and remembers that in this browser only.

How the lists are built

The universe is every patent family filed in 2013–2022 that the LMICinnovation pipeline links to a Scoreboard firm (firmmap_2025, 2,905,179 families, of which 76,071 involve at least one EMDE-excl.-China inventor and 4,853 of those are green). Values come from bigX_family_level: knowledge spillovers (ev_*) and marginal returns (istrax_*) by recipient group, and private value (pv), all as in the paper. A family linked to several Scoreboard firms counts for each of them in the firm averages and is listed once, with all its firms, in the innovation lists. The country composition is the family’s row set in iseapp’s countrymap (every country of an inventor or applicant after the name-based harmonisation of build_countries_harm_duck.R), which is exactly the input from which innopaper_results1.rmd derives the HICinno / CNinno / EMDENOCNinno flags; 0 of the families here have a flag that does not agree with this table. The raw inventor records (inventors_2025, persons_2025, persons_addr_inferred) feed the donut (inventors by country of residence; records without a country code in grey). Headlines and summaries (patent_summaries.json) are non-technical paraphrases of the title and abstract written by Claude; drawings are the first figure Google Patents holds for the family, hot-linked from Google’s patent image store, taken from a family member when the fetched publication has none. The EMDERLT samples use mnc_rd_labs_data/emde_rd_labs_map.json (1,350 verified labs outside China): an innovation is lab-linked when one of its Scoreboard firms has a verified lab in an EMDE country on the family’s record — 42,736 innovations, 2,967 of them green. Publication numbers are those the Innovation Strategy Explorer stores per family; titles and abstracts were retrieved from Google Patents on 12 October 2026 for the 818 families that appear in a list. Flat CSVs of every list are in _cache_emde_inno_examples/. Built 12 October 2026.
